nodes.name: Ni-P Chemical Plating on NF
nodes.procedure: The NF substrate (3 cm×6 cm) was degreased with acetone for 15 min, and then etched with 2 M HCl for 15 min before plating. The chemical-Plating solution was consisted with NiSO4·6H2O 25 gL^{-1}, NaH2PO2·H2O 25 gL^{-1}, CH3COONa·3H2O 15 gL^{-1}, and C6H5Na3O7 15 gL^{-1}. And the pH of the solution was adjusted to be 4.5 with concentrated sulfuric acid titration. Then, NF was inserted vertically into the plating solution at 80°C for 10, 30, 60, 90, and 120 min. After plating, Ni-P/NF was cleaned by distilled water and dried at 60°C for 6 h.

nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Nickel Phosphorus Compounds (Ni-P/NF) on NF: Ni-P/NF was prepared by chemical-plating of Ni-P alloy on NF.

nodes.name: NiFe LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The solution was consisted with 2 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 4 mmol NH4F and 10 mmol urea. The NF and the mixed solution were transferred to a 100 mL autoclave. NiFe LDH nanosheets were obtained after heated the autoclave at 120°C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiFe LDH Nanosheets: NiFe LDH nanosheets were grown directly on NF by hydrothermal method.

nodes.name: P-doped NiFe LDH Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFePx LDH nanosheets were grown on Ni-P/NF by hydrothermal method. The solution was consisted with 2 mmol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 2 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 4 mmol NH4F and 10 mmol urea. Then Ni-P/NF and the mixed solution were transferred to a 100 mL autoclave. NiFePx LDH nanosheets were obtained after heated the autoclave at 120°C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of P-Doped NiFe LDH Nanosheets (NiFePx LDH): NiFePx LDH nanosheets were grown on Ni-P/NF by hydrothermal method.

nodes.characterization_summary: P contents determined as 0.15, 0.24, and 0.32 wt.% for NiFeP_x LDH with chemical plating times of 10, 30, and 60 min respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the corresponding P contents in NiFeP_x LDH nanosheets is 0.15, 0.24, and 0.32 wt.% by inductive coupled plasma (ICP)-OES results (Table S1, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH shows nanosheet morphology similar to NiFeP_{0.15} LDH, NiFeP_{0.24} LDH, and NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH showed the nanosheet morphology as that of NiFeP_{0.15} LDH, NiFeP_{0.24} LDH, and NiFe LDH

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH exhibits lamellar nanosheet morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image shown in Figure 1c further reveals the lamellar nanosheet morphology of NiFeP_{0.32} LDH.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH shows lattice distances of 0.225 nm and 0.181 nm corresponding to (015) and (018) crystal planes, smaller than theoretical values of 0.2308 nm and 0.1972 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice distances of 0.225 and 0.181 nm, obtained from the profile map of the spacing between crystal plane spacing ... correspond to the (015) and (018) crystal planes of NiFeP_{0.32} LDH, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, and P elements confirmed in NiFeP_{0.32} LDH; P element existence verified.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distribution of Ni, Fe, and P elements for NiFeP_{0.32} LDH was explored (Figure 1e). ... The existence of P element was also confirmed by Energy Dispersive Spectrometer (EDS) element analysis

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic peaks of NiFe LDH at 11.11°, 22.64°, 33.54°, 34.09°, 38.59°, 45.90°, 59.58°, and 60.84° assigned to (003), (006), (012), (009), (015), (018), (110), and (113) planes; NiFeP_x LDH shows same peaks shifted to higher angles indicating lattice contraction; no new crystal phases observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of NiFeP_x LDH was characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Figure 2a, the characteristic peaks of NiFe LDH at two theta = 11.11°, 22.64°, 33.54°, 34.09°, 38.59°, 45.90°, 59.58°, and 60.84° are assigned to the (003), (006), (012), (009), (015), (018), (110), and (113) crystal planes respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH confirms presence of P element; Ni 2p peaks at 855.8 eV (Ni^{2+} 2p_{3/2}) and 873.59 eV (Ni^{2+} 2p_{1/2}); Fe 2p shifts to higher binding energy indicating modified chemical environment (main peaks at 713.6 eV and 727.08 eV for Fe^{3+}); P 2p shows oxidized P at 133.31 eV and P-M coordination at 129.1 eV, 130.1 eV; O 1s peaks at ≈529.6 eV (M-O), 531.3 eV (hydroxyl/surface oxygen), 533.3 eV (P-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed to investigate the chemical composition and electronic structure of NiFe LDH and NiFeP_{0.32} LDH. ... The P 2p spectrum of NiFeP_{0.32} LDH (Figure 2d) exhibits a peak at 133.31 eV, attributing to the oxidized P state. And the peaks at 129.1 and 130.1 eV, which belong to the P-M peaks

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES shows positive shifted absorption edge for NiFeP_{0.32} LDH indicating increased Fe valence; Fe-O bond length larger in NiFeP_{0.32} LDH; wavelet transforms confirm Fe-P bonds with peaks at 5.9 and 8.2 Å^{-1}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination bonding of NiFeP_{0.32} LDH was also verified by Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH shows highest C_{dl} value of 5.2 mF cm^{-2} indicating abundant electrochemical surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The highest C_{dl} value (5.2 mF cm^{-2}) of NiFeP_{0.32} LDH suggests an abundant electrochemical surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeP_{0.32} LDH exhibits smallest impedance indicating fastest charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFeP_{0.32} LDH electrocatalyst exhibits the smallest impedance among other NiFeP_x LDH electrocatalysts

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR results confirm P insertion into NiFe LDH structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR results also prove that P has been inserted into LDH (Figure S9, Supporting Information).
